correctness.rationale: For every fixed integer m>=3, exact normalized beta moments and orthogonality of residual angular frequencies yield a diagonal norm identity. The second-order product expansion has explicit coefficient F_m and G_m, verified algebraically and with 2,175 exact rational assertions. An explicit telescoping-product bound excludes both n/alpha->0 and n/alpha->infinity; C1-uniform interior expansions and strict concavity at the unique peak localize every maximizer within O_m(1) indices. G_m((m-1)/2)=-F_m((m-1)/2) proves the universal second-order correction. The proof does not confuse finite checking with asymptotic certification.

value.rationale: Provides an entire family of sharp weighted analytic-approximation asymptotics, not a finite sample or a single higher monomial. For every fixed m>=3 it identifies the unique scaled mode at which the global operator norm concentrates and an explicit spectral profile, while proving the non-obvious universal cancellation of the first correction in (alpha+1) times the squared norm. These constants quantify reconstruction/approximation stability across changing Bergman weight and link the optimal index with the hyperbolic radius r^2=(m-1)/(m+1). The result does not purport to be a general-symbol theorem.
